children.name: Seseli salsugineum A.Duran & Lyskov
children.description: Distribution and ecology: — Seseli salsugineum is a narrow endemic species, confined to Lake Tuz Gölü area (Konya province) in Central Anatolia, Turkey. children.name: Physospermopsis
children.description: Physospermopsis — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Physospermopsis alepidioides  R.H.Shan
children.description: Diagnostic characters. Physospermopsis alepidioides usually possesses an entire leaf blade with a sparsely serrated margin. The shape of the entire leaf segment is an obvious diagnostic characteristic to distinguish it from other Physospermopsis species. The stem of it is velutinous.

children.name: Physospermopsis delavayi  H.Wolff
children.description: Diagnostic characters. P. delavayi usually possesses a conspicuously winged rachis and yellow-green, round fruits. The bracts are usually smaller than other species of Physospermopsis. The basal leaves are obovate to obovate-orbicular with incised-serrate or lobed margin or cuneate with partite margin.

children.name: Physospermopsis handelii  Pimenov & Kljuykov
children.description: The native range of this species is China (NW. Yunnan) to NE. Myanmar. It is a perennial and grows primarily in the subalpine or subarctic biome.

children.name: Physospermopsis kingdon-wardii  C.Norman
children.description: Diagnostic characters. P. kingdon-wardii is similar to P. obtusiuscula in shape of basal leaves, but the stem of P. kingdon-wardii is reduced. The fruits are smaller than other species, and the immature fruits sometimes have sparse minute warts. Additionally, the ribs are prominent, often sinuate.

children.name: Physospermopsis muliensis R.H.Shan & S.L.Liou
children.description: Diagnostic characters. Physospermopsis muliensis usually possesses branching stems, ovate-oblong leaf blades, narrow sheaths, leaf-like bracts, lanceolate bracteoles, and ovoid fruits with filiform ribs with sparse scattered warts. Basal and lower petioles are narrowly winged.

children.name: Physospermopsis nana  Pimenov & Kljuykov
children.description: Diagnostic characters. Physospermopsis nana usually possesses reduced stem, membranous-margined sheaths, and leaf-like bracts. The bracteoles are pale green with whitish margin in lower half. The ultimate segments are linear-lanceolate. The characters mentioned above are sufficient to distinguish it from other Physospermopsis species.

children.name: Physospermopsis obtusiuscula  C.Norman
children.description: Diagnostic characters. Physospermopsis obtusiuscula sometimes is flushed. The stems are dark purple-green, simple, and occasionally branched at the base. The fruit ribs are narrowly winged and sinuolate, which is a unique character in Physospermopsis.

children.name: Physospermopsis rubrinervis  C.Norman
children.description: Diagnostic characters. Physospermopsis rubrinervis usually possesses dark purple, sparsely branching stems. The basal blade is ovate to broadly ovate in outline, having almost purple-red nerves.
